title: Miniature Mini Golf Diorama
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a miniature mini golf diorama game using Three.js. The scene is a tabletop-scale mini golf hole viewed from a slightly elevated perspective.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 8, 12) looking at (0, 0, 0).
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8 and castShadow enabled.
- The renderer should have shadow mapping enabled and a soft sky-blue background (#87CEEB).

## Golf Course
- Create a rectangular green fairway (plane geometry, 4 wide x 12 long, green color #2d8a4e) centered at origin, lying flat on Y=0.
- Add raised brown wooden borders (thin box geometries, color #8B4513) around all four edges of the fairway, height 0.3.
- Place a hole (small black cylinder, radius 0.3, depth 0.1) at position (0, 0.01, -4.5) on the fairway.
- Add a small red flag (thin cylinder pole + small triangle flag) at the hole position, pole height 1.5.
- Place two rectangular obstacle bumpers (box geometry, color #A0522D, size roughly 1.5x0.4x0.3) at positions (-0.8, 0.15, -1.5) rotated 20 degrees and (1.0, 0.15, -2.8) rotated -15 degrees.

## 3D Asset
- Load 'Lantern.glb' using GLTFLoader. Place the lantern model at position (2.5, 0, 1.0) beside the fairway as a decorative diorama element. Scale it to fit the miniature scene (scale ~0.5). The lantern should cast shadows.

## Golf Ball
- Create a white sphere (radius 0.15) as the golf ball, starting at position (0, 0.15, 4.5) — the tee position.
- The ball should cast shadows.

## Aiming & Power System
- Display a dashed aim line from the ball in the current aim direction (default: straight toward hole, i.e., negative Z).
- Arrow Left/Right keys rotate the aim direction by 5 degrees per press.
- A power bar is shown in the HUD (bottom center). Pressing and holding Space increases power from 0 to 100 over 2 seconds. Releasing Space triggers the shot.
- The aim line should update in real-time as the player rotates.

## Ball Physics
- After a shot, the ball moves in the aimed direction with initial velocity proportional to power (max speed ~8 units/sec).
- Apply friction deceleration of 0.98 multiplier per frame so the ball slows and stops.
- The ball must bounce off the wooden borders and obstacle bumpers (simple reflection: invert the appropriate velocity component).
- The ball stays on the fairway plane (Y = 0.15 always).
- When the ball's speed drops below 0.05, it stops completely and the player can aim again.

## Hole Detection
- If the ball center is within 0.3 units of the hole center AND speed < 1.0, the ball is 'sunk'. Play a success state.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left: 'Stroke: X' counter (starts at 0, increments each shot).
- Top-right: 'Par: 2' static label.
- Bottom-center: Power bar (a div, 200px wide, 20px tall, border). Fill width proportional to current power, colored gradient from green (low) to red (high).
- When the ball is sunk, show a centered overlay 'Hole in X!' message and a 'Play Again' button that resets everything.
- A 'Reset Ball' button in top-center that returns the ball to tee position without changing stroke count.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- ballPosition: {x, y, z} — current ball position
- ballSpeed: number — current ball speed magnitude
- ballMoving: boolean — whether ball is currently in motion
- aimAngle: number — current aim angle in degrees (0 = straight toward hole / -Z)
- power: number — current power level 0-100
- strokeCount: number — total shots taken
- holeSunk: boolean — whether ball has been sunk
- lanternLoaded: boolean — whether Lantern.glb loaded successfully
- gamePhase: 'aiming' | 'charging' | 'rolling' | 'sunk'

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame during the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Ball friction deceleration factor 0.98/frame. Ball reflects off borders and bumpers. Ball constrained to fairway plane Y=0.15. Hole sunk when distance < 0.3 and speed < 1.0. Max initial velocity ~8 units/sec at power 100.
